Chrysler Gets Flak For Patching Hack Via Mailed USB
Seems like a pretty safe way to do it. Much safer than sending it remotely...

The problem is that mailing someone a USB drive and saying "hey, plug this into your car" is a really shortsighted way to deliver updates. Having people plug in USB drives should be something you strongly discourage, not rely on for update distribution. What amuses me is that the vulnerability itself is exploited by hackers connecting to the vehicle over the internet and pushing custom firmware to the embedded system. Yet Chrysler cannot itself push the security update through the same way.

I have mixed feeling on this. On one hand, USB deployment is sketchy. But on the other hand, this is probably the quickest way to get the patch to customers (particularly ones who won't bother to come to a dealership if asked). I would hope that their software is able to verify firmware images via a digital signature.
